summaryEn: A long, personal conversation with Indian entrepreneur Nikhil Kamath on work, consciousness, family, money, AI, India and how the future might unfold.
summaryZh: 与印度企业家尼基尔·卡马特进行的一场漫长而私人的对话，涉及工作、意识、家庭、金钱、AI、印度以及未来可能如何展开。

segments.textEn: Our audience is largely want to be entrepreneurs in India. And I feel like all of us have so much to learn from you because you've done it so many times over in so many different domains. So, we will speak to them today, and I will try and centre all my questions in that direction so they can take advantage of this conversation and maybe start-- take a chance and build something. Do you want a coffee? Um... -Sure, why not? -Okay.
segments.textZh: 我们的观众主要是印度那些想成为企业家的人。我觉得我们所有人都有太多东西可以向你学习，因为你已经在如此多不同领域一次又一次地做成了。所以，我们今天会面向他们交流，我会尽量让我的所有问题都围绕这个方向展开，这样他们就能从这场对话中受益，也许会开始——冒一次险，做出点东西。你想喝咖啡吗？嗯……——当然，为什么不呢？——好。

segments.textEn: Are we gonna be talking for a while? -[laughs] -I hope we are. Okay, good. Sure. -Um... -Meghana? May I trouble you for a coffee? Can we get another coffee? -[Meghana] Anything's fine? -Uh... Cappuccino, I guess. [Meghana] Cappuccino? Okay. Are you a coffee drinker, Elon? -Yeah, yeah. -Yeah? Yeah, I have a coffee once, -usually in the mornings. -Okay. -One-a-day kind of thing? -Yeah, pretty much. You want to wait for it? No, I'm good.
segments.textZh: 我们会聊一阵子吗？——[笑]——我希望会。好，很好。当然。——嗯……——Meghana？能麻烦你给我一杯咖啡吗？我们能再来一杯咖啡吗？——[Meghana] 什么都可以吗？——呃……我想要卡布奇诺。[Meghana] 卡布奇诺？好的。埃隆，你喝咖啡吗？——对，对。——是吗？对，我喝一杯咖啡，——通常是在早上。——好。——每天一杯那种？——对，差不多。你想等咖啡来吗？不用，我没事。

segments.textEn: [laughter] The first thing I must say is you're a lot bigger and bulkier, muscular, than I would have thought you are. Oh, stop, you're making me blush. Really. Seriously. Yeah, I mean, look, on the Internet, I'm small, you know? You're essentially... What percentage of Internet is spent on Twitter? Is there a number to it? On X. Well, so, we have, like, about 600 million monthly users.
segments.textZh: [笑声] 我首先必须说，你比我原以为的高大壮实得多，也更有肌肉。哦，别说了，你都让我脸红了。真的。说真的。对，我是说，你看，在互联网上，我很小，你知道吧？你基本上……互联网上有多大比例的时间花在Twitter上？这有具体数字吗？在X上。嗯，这个，我们每月大约有6亿用户。

segments.textEn: Although, it can spike up, if there's some major event in the world. It can get up to, I don't know, 800 million or a billion, if there's some major event in the world, so... I don't know, 250 to 300 million per week type of thing. It's a pretty decent number. It tends to be readers, you know, people that read words. You know, so... Do you think that'll change? Yeah, I mean, there's... There's certainly a lot of video on the X system.
segments.textZh: 不过，如果世界上发生某个重大事件，这个数字可能会猛增。如果世界上发生某个重大事件，它可能会达到，我不知道，8亿或10亿，所以……我不知道，每周大概2.5亿到3亿。这是一个相当可观的数字。用户往往是读者，你知道，就是那些阅读文字的人。你知道，所以……你觉得这会改变吗？会，我是说，有……X系统上当然有大量视频。

segments.textEn: But at this point... Increasing amounts of video. But I think where the X network is strongest is among people who think a lot and read a lot. You know, so, that's where it's gonna be strongest. Because we have words. And, you know, so... Among readers, writers, and thinkers, I think X is number one in the world. As far as social media goes, the form factor, if you had to wager a guess for tomorrow... -Yeah. -...
segments.textZh: 但目前……视频数量越来越多。但我认为X网络最强的地方，是在那些思考很多、阅读很多的人群当中。你知道，所以，那里会是它最强的地方。因为我们有文字。而且，你知道，所以……在读者、作者和思考者当中，我认为X是世界第一。就社交媒体而言，如果你必须猜一猜明天的形态……——对。——……

segments.textEn: how much is text, how much is video? I've heard you speak about maybe voice and hearing being the next form of communication with AI. What happens to X in its true form? How does it evolve? Yeah, so, I do think most interaction is gonna be video in the future. Most interactions are gonna be real-time video with AI. So, real-time video comprehension, real-time video generation, that's gonna be most of the load.
segments.textZh: 文字占多少，视频占多少？我听你谈到过，也许语音和听觉会成为与AI交流的下一种形式。X的真正形态会发生什么变化？它会如何演进？对，所以，我确实认为未来大多数互动都会是视频。大多数互动都会是与AI进行的实时视频互动。所以，实时视频理解、实时视频生成，这将占据大部分负载。

segments.textEn: And that's how it is for most of the Internet right now. Most of the Internet is video. Text is a pretty small percentage. But the text tends to be higher value, generally. Or more, it's more densely compressed information. Yeah, so... But if you say what is the most amount of bits generated and compute spent, it's certainly gonna be video. So, I used to be a shareholder of X, -a very small one. -Okay.
segments.textZh: 而现在互联网的大部分也是这样。互联网的大部分内容都是视频。文字所占比例相当小。但总体而言，文字往往价值更高。或者说，它是更加密集压缩的信息。对，所以……但如果你问生成的比特总量和花费的算力最多的是什么，那肯定会是视频。所以，我以前是X的股东，——一个非常小的股东。——好。

segments.textEn: And I got paid when you bought Twitter and you made it X. -Happy decision? Glad you did it? -Yeah, yeah, I think it was important. You know, I felt like Twitter was heading in... or had gone in a direction that had more of a negative influence on the world. It was... I mean, of course, this depends on one's perspective. Some people will say, well, actually, they liked the way it was, and now, they don't like it.
segments.textZh: 你收购Twitter并把它变成X时，我拿到了钱。——这是个令人满意的决定吗？你庆幸自己这么做了吗？——对，对，我认为这很重要。你知道，我觉得Twitter正朝着……或者已经走向了一个对世界产生了更多负面影响的方向。它……我是说，当然，这取决于一个人的视角。有些人会说，嗯，实际上，他们喜欢它以前的样子，而现在，他们不喜欢了。

segments.textEn: But I think the fundamental thing was that... Twitter was amplifying... I would say, a fairly pretty far left by most people's standards in the world's ideology because of where it was based, in San Francisco. And then they actually suspended a lot of people on the right. So, from their perspective, even someone in the centre would be far right. If you're far left, anyone in the centre is far right, because...
segments.textZh: 但我认为根本问题在于……Twitter在放大……我会说，按照世界上大多数人的标准，那是一种相当、相当极左的意识形态，因为它所在地的缘故，也就是旧金山。然后他们实际上封禁了很多右翼人士。所以，从他们的视角来看，即便是中间派人士也会是极右翼。如果你是极左派，那么任何中间派人士都是极右翼，因为……

segments.textEn: It's just on the political spectrum, they're just as far left as you get in the United States and in San Francisco. So, what I've tried to do is just restore it to be balanced and centrist. So, there haven't been any left-wing voices that have been suspended or banned or de-amplified or anything like that. Now, some of them have chosen to just go somewhere else, but...
segments.textZh: 这只是政治光谱的问题，他们已经处于美国和旧金山所能达到的最左端。所以，我一直试图做的，就是恢复它的平衡与中间立场。所以，没有任何左翼声音遭到封禁、禁止、降低传播权重或任何类似处理。现在，其中一些人选择直接去别处了，但……

segments.textEn: But at this point, the operating principle of the X system is to adhere to any country's laws, but not to put our thumb on the scale beyond the laws of a country. When I think of social media... -Oh, thank you. -Thank you. When I think of social media, Elon, I feel like... even data suggests that the current incumbents seem to be losing traction amongst the youngest of audience. Yeah. Even platforms like Instagram...
segments.textZh: 但目前，X系统的运作原则是遵守任何国家的法律，但不会在一个国家的法律之外人为影响天平。当我想到社交媒体时……——哦，谢谢。——谢谢。当我想到社交媒体时，埃隆，我觉得……甚至数据也表明，目前的既有平台似乎正在失去最年轻受众的关注。对。即便是Instagram这样的平台……

segments.textEn: I mean, they're not exactly like Twitter, but platforms across the board. If one had to rework social media and build something bottom-up, what do you think would work for the world of tomorrow? Well, I mean, I don't think that much about... about social media, to be frank. I mean, it's... I mostly just wanna have something where there's...
segments.textZh: 我是说，它们并不完全像Twitter，但各类平台都是如此。如果要重新构建社交媒体，并自下而上地打造某种东西，你认为在未来的世界里什么会奏效？嗯，我是说，坦白讲，我没有太多考虑……考虑社交媒体。我是说，它……我主要只是想要一个其中存在……

segments.textEn: in the case of X, kind of a global town square, where people can say what they wanna say with words, pictures, video... where there's a secure messaging system. We've recently added the ability to do audio and video calls. So, really trying to bring the world together into a eclectic consciousness. That's, I guess, different from just saying, like, "What is the most dopamine-generating video stream that one could make?"
segments.textZh: 就X而言，某种全球城市广场，人们可以用文字、图片、视频……表达他们想说的话……那里有安全的消息系统。我们最近新增了进行音频和视频通话的功能。所以，我们实际上是在努力把世界汇聚成一种兼容并蓄的意识。我想，这不同于只是说，比如，“人们能制作出的最能产生多巴胺的视频流是什么？”

segments.textEn: Which, you know, I think it can be a little bit of brain rot, frankly. You know, if you're just watching videos that just cause dopamine hits one after another, but lack substance, then I think those are not great. That's not a great way to spend time. But I do think that's actually what a lot of people are gonna wanna watch. So, if you say, like, total Internet usage, it's gonna probably be optimising for, you know, neurotransmitter generation.
segments.textZh: 这个，你知道，坦白讲，我认为它可能有点让人脑子坏掉。你知道，如果你只是在看那些一次又一次激发多巴胺、却缺乏实质内容的视频，那么我认为那些东西不太好。那不是一种很好的时间使用方式。但我确实认为，那实际上会是很多人想看的东西。所以，如果你说，比如，互联网总使用量，它很可能会针对，你知道，神经递质的产生进行优化。

segments.textEn: Like, there's somebody getting a kick out of it. But it becomes like a drug type of thing. But I'm not really after... My goal is not to do that. I guess I could do that if I wanted to, but, um, I... I just wanna really have a global platform that brings together... Like I said, it becomes close to, sort of, a collective consciousness of humanity as possible. And one of the things that we've introduced, um, for example, is automatic translation.
segments.textZh: 就像，有人会从中获得快感。但它会变成类似毒品的东西。但我真正追求的并不是……我的目标并不是做那个。我想，如果我愿意，我可以那么做，但，嗯，我……我真的只是想拥有一个全球性平台，把……汇聚到一起。就像我说的，它会尽可能接近某种人类的集体意识。而我们已经引入的东西之一，嗯，例如，就是自动翻译。

segments.textEn: 'Cause I think it would be great to bring together what people say in many different languages, and... but automatically translated for the recipient. So, you have the collective consciousness, not just of, say, people in a particular language group, but you have the thoughts of people in, you know, every language group. And why is that important, Elon? Collective consciousness, to have one platform? I guess... Yeah, why is that important?
segments.textZh: 因为我认为，把人们用许多不同语言说的话汇聚到一起会很棒，而且……但会为接收者自动翻译。这样，你所拥有的集体意识就不只是，比如，某个特定语言群体中人们的集体意识，而是拥有，你知道，每个语言群体中人们的思想。埃隆，为什么这很重要？集体意识，拥有一个平台？我想……对，为什么这很重要？

segments.textEn: I guess it's-- You could also say, like, why... You know, if you consider humans, like, humans are composed of around 30 to 40 trillion cells. You know, there's trillions of synapses in your mind. But there's not-- The why of it, I mean, I guess, it's just so we can increase... our understanding. Increase our... our understanding of the universe. I guess I had this... sort of question about what's the meaning of life, you know?
segments.textZh: 我想这是——你也可以说，比如，为什么……你知道，如果你考虑人类，比如，人类由大约30万亿至40万亿个细胞组成。你知道，你的头脑中有数万亿个突触。但并没有——至于为什么，我是说，我想，只是为了让我们能够增进……我们的理解。增进我们……我们对宇宙的理解。我想我曾有过这个……关于生命的意义是什么之类的问题，你知道吗？

segments.textEn: Why is anything important? You know, why are we here? What's the origin of the universe? What is the end? What are the questions that we don't even know to ask? And probably the questions we don't even know to ask are the most important ones. So, I'm just trying to, I guess, understand what's going on. What is going on in this reality? Is this reality? And where did you get when you asked, "What is the point of life?" Yeah, so, I...
segments.textZh: 为什么任何事物都重要？你知道，我们为什么在这里？宇宙的起源是什么？终点是什么？有哪些问题是我们甚至不知道该去问的？而且，我们甚至不知道该问的问题，可能才是最重要的。所以，我只是想，我想，弄明白发生了什么。这个现实中正在发生什么？这是现实吗？而当你问“生命的意义是什么？”时，你得出了什么？是的，所以，我……

segments.textEn: I came to the conclusion that... which is somewhat, in the Douglas Adams Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy school of thought, -which is-- -42. Yeah, you know, he sort of... Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy is like a book on philosophy disguised as humour. -Yeah. -And... That's where you get the-- You know, Earth turns out to be this computer to understand, to get to figure out the answer of the meaning of life.
segments.textZh: 我得出的结论是……这多少属于道格拉斯·亚当斯《银河系漫游指南》那一派的思想，——也就是——42。是的，你知道，他有点……《银河系漫游指南》就像是一本伪装成幽默作品的哲学书。——是的。——而且……你就是从那里得到那个——你知道，地球结果是这样一台计算机，用来理解、用来设法找出生命意义的答案。

segments.textEn: And it comes up with the answer of 42. But then, it's like, "What does 42 mean?" And it turns out, well, actually, the hard part is the question, not the answer. And for that, you need a much bigger computer than Earth. So, basically, what Douglas Adams was saying is that we actually don't know how to frame the questions properly.
segments.textZh: 而它得出的答案是42。但然后，问题就成了：“42是什么意思？”结果发现，嗯，实际上，困难的部分是问题，而不是答案。为此，你需要一台比地球大得多的计算机。所以，基本上，道格拉斯·亚当斯所说的是，我们其实不知道如何正确地构建问题。

segments.textEn: And so, I think by expanding the scope and scale of consciousness, we can better understand what questions to ask about the answer that is the universe. Do you believe the collective consciousness of society-- I was watching this movie recently called the Gladiator. -Russell Crowe. Have you seen it? -Yeah, yeah. In Gladiator, in Rome, when people are fighting, and the crowd is cheering when people kill each other...
segments.textZh: 所以，我认为，通过扩大意识的范围和规模，我们可以更好地理解，面对宇宙这个答案，该提出什么问题。你相信社会的集体意识——我最近在看一部叫《角斗士》的电影。——罗素·克劳。你看过吗？——是的，是的。在《角斗士》里，在罗马，当人们打斗，而人群在人们互相残杀时欢呼……

segments.textEn: the collective is very much like the mob. It doesn't have nuance in its opinion, per se. That's this particular kind of mob. I mean, they're sort of going there to see people kill each other, you know? Do you suspect the society we live in today is very different? We don't, generally-- At this point, we don't... you know, go and watch people kill each other. [laughter] Maybe some kind of euphemism of that. -Sports, I suppose. -Mm.
segments.textZh: 这个集体非常像暴民。可以说，它的观点缺乏细微差别。那是这种特定类型的暴民。我是说，他们去那里就是为了看人们互相残杀，你知道吗？你是否认为我们今天生活的社会非常不同？我们通常不会——到了这个时候，我们不会……你知道，去看人们互相残杀。[笑声]也许会看那件事的某种委婉版本。——我想是体育。——嗯。

segments.textEn: So, people do sports without-- where teams attempt to defeat each other, -but minus the death. -Right. Just going back to the consideration of a human. We all started out as one cell, but now, we are... over 30 trillion cells. But I think most people feel like they're one body. Like, you know, usually, your right hand's not fighting your left hand type of thing, you know? They just sort of cooperate. Your mind is... you know...
segments.textZh: 所以，人们进行体育运动而不会——在其中，各支队伍试图击败彼此，——但没有死亡。——对。再回到对一个人的考量。我们最初都是1个细胞，但现在，我们有……超过30万亿个细胞。但我想，大多数人都觉得自己是1个身体。比如，你知道，通常不会发生你的右手和左手打架之类的事，你知道吗？它们就是以某种方式合作。你的头脑是……你知道……

segments.textEn: just a vast number of neurons. But most of the time, it doesn't feel like there's, you know, a trillion voices in your brain. Hopefully not. So, there's clearly more that happens when you have trillions of cells working as a cellular collective than, say, one cell. Or a small, you know, small multicellular creature. There's clearly something different that happens. Like, you can't talk to a bacteria, you know? -Yeah. -Yeah. It's very silent.
segments.textZh: 只不过是数量极其庞大的神经元。但大多数时候，你不会觉得，你知道，自己的大脑里有1万亿个声音。希望没有。所以，当数万亿个细胞作为一个细胞集体共同工作时，显然会发生比方说1个细胞，或一个很小的、你知道，很小的多细胞生物所不会发生的更多事情。显然会发生一些不同的事。比如，你没法和一个细菌交谈，你知道吗？——是的。——是的。它非常安静。

segments.textEn: They just sort of wiggle around, and... From their perspective, I don't know. I just thought of what is life like from the perspective of an amoeba, you know? But I know you can't talk to an amoeba. Like, they don't talk back. But you can talk to humans. So, there's just something, obviously, qualitatively fundamentally different for humans. Once you have a large number of cells, and, you know, sufficiently large brain type of thing, there's...
segments.textZh: 它们只是在四处扭动，然后……从它们的角度来看，我不知道。我只是想到，从一只变形虫的角度看，生命是什么样的，你知道吗？但我知道你没法和变形虫说话。比如，它们不会回应。但你可以和人类交谈。所以，对人类而言，显然存在某种性质上根本不同的东西。一旦你拥有大量细胞，以及，你知道，足够大的大脑之类的，就会有……

segments.textEn: you can now talk to humans. And they can say things, they can produce things. But bacteria are not gonna produce a spaceship, for example. But humans can. So I think there's something qualitatively different that also happens when there's a collection of humans. In fact, it's safe to say that a single human cannot make a spaceship. I cannot make a spaceship by myself. But with a collection of humans, we can make spaceships.
segments.textZh: 你现在可以和人类交谈了。而且他们可以说话，可以制造东西。但比如说，细菌不会制造出宇宙飞船。但人类可以。所以我认为，当人类聚集在一起时，也会发生某种性质上的不同。事实上，可以肯定地说，单个人类无法制造宇宙飞船。我无法独自制造宇宙飞船。但一群人聚集在一起，我们就可以制造宇宙飞船。

segments.textEn: So, there's something, obviously, qualitatively different about a collection of humans. In fact, it would be impossible for me to learn all of the areas of expertise. There wouldn't be enough time in one lifetime to even learn all the things before I was dead. So, you really fundamentally have to have a collection of humans to make a rocket. Then, I think there are probably some other scaling...
segments.textZh: 所以，一群人聚集在一起显然存在某种性质上的不同。事实上，我不可能学会所有专业领域的知识。即便要在我死前学会所有那些东西，一生的时间也不够。所以，从根本上说，你确实必须有一群人才能制造火箭。然后，我认为可能还有其他一些规模扩大……

segments.textEn: qualitative scaling things that happen when you have groups of humans. And then, if the quality of the interaction, or the quality of the information flow... the better it is, the more the human collective will achieve. And, like I said, I'm just curious about the nature of the universe.
segments.textZh: 当人类组成群体时会发生的性质上的规模效应。然后，如果互动的质量，或者信息流的质量……越好，人类集体取得的成就就越大。而且，就像我说的，我只是对宇宙的本质感到好奇。

segments.textEn: And I think if we-- It's safe to say, like, if we increase the scope and scale of consciousness, we're much more likely to understand the nature of the universe than if we reduce it. Is that a bit like spirituality? A lot of people talk to me about spirituality. Right. I still don't know what it actually means. Like, I keep asking them, "What do you mean?" Yeah. "What do you mean?" I mean, a lot of people have spiritual feelings. Right.
segments.textZh: 而且我认为，如果我们——可以肯定地说，比如，如果我们扩大意识的范围和规模，那么相比缩小它，我们理解宇宙本质的可能性要大得多。这有点像灵性吗？很多人会跟我谈灵性。对。我仍然不知道它实际上是什么意思。比如，我一直问他们：“你是什么意思？”是啊。“你是什么意思？”我的意思是，很多人都有灵性感受。对。

segments.textEn: And I wouldn't try to deny that those spiritual feelings are real to them. But it's... It doesn't entirely translate. Just because somebody else has a spiritual feeling doesn't mean that I would have that spiritual feeling. You know, I tend to be kind of physics-pulled, which is, like, if something has predictive value, then... I'll pay more attention to it than if it doesn't have predictive value. Right.
segments.textZh: 而且我不会试图否认，那些灵性感受对他们来说是真实的。但这……并不能完全转化过来。仅仅因为别人有一种灵性感受，并不意味着我也会有那种灵性感受。你知道，我往往有点受物理学牵引，也就是说，如果某样东西具有预测价值，那么……相比不具备预测价值的东西，我会更关注它。对。

segments.textEn: So, you know, physics, I would say, is the study of that which has predictive value. I think it's a pretty good definition. My primary job, Elon, is a stockbroker and stock investor. -Okay. -There is no predictive value. Nobody knows what will happen tomorrow. Well, but I think you can generally say, you know, that... If it's long-term for a company, then you can say, like, "Do you like the products or services of that company?
segments.textZh: 所以，你知道，我会说，物理学就是研究那些具有预测价值的事物。我觉得这是个相当不错的定义。埃隆，我的主要工作是股票经纪人和股票投资者。——好的。——这里没有预测价值。没人知道明天会发生什么。嗯，但我认为，一般来说，你可以这么说，你知道……如果是从一家公司的长期来看，那么你可以问，比如：“你喜欢那家公司的产品或服务吗？

segments.textEn: And is it likely to... Do you like the product roadmap? Do you like-- It seems like they make great products and they're likely to make great products in the future." If that's the case, then I would say that's probably a good company to invest in. And I think you also want to believe in the team.
segments.textZh: 而且它是否有可能……你喜欢它的产品路线图吗？你喜欢——它们似乎制造出了很棒的产品，而且将来很可能也会制造出很棒的产品。”如果是这样，那么我会说，那可能是一家值得投资的好公司。而且我认为你还应该信任这个团队。

segments.textEn: So if you're like, "Well, that's a talented and hardworking team, they make good products today, they seem to be still motivated to make things in the future." Then I'd say that's a good company to invest in. Fair point. Yeah, and now, that... That won't solve for the daily fluctuations which happen, and, sometimes, are pretty extreme. But over time, that is the right way to invest in stocks.
segments.textZh: 所以，如果你说：“嗯，那是一支有才华又勤奋的团队，他们现在做出了好产品，看起来仍然有动力在未来继续做东西。”那么我会说，那是一家值得投资的好公司。说得有道理。对，而现在，那个……那解决不了每天发生的波动，而这些波动有时会相当剧烈。但从长期来看，那才是投资股票的正确方式。

segments.textEn: Because a company is just a group of people assembled to create products and services. So you have to say, "Well, what other-- How good are those products and services? Are they likely to continue to improve in the future?" If so, then you should buy the stock of that company and then don't worry too much about the daily fluctuations. Right. What's got you most excited now, Elon, in terms of all that you're building? You're doing so much.
segments.textZh: 因为公司只是一群聚集在一起创造产品和服务的人。所以你必须问：“嗯，还有什么——那些产品和服务有多好？它们未来可能会继续改进吗？”如果是，那么你应该买那家公司的股票，然后不要太担心每天的波动。对。埃隆，就你正在打造的这一切而言，现在最让你兴奋的是什么？你正在做这么多事情。

segments.textEn: So let me just preface and contextualise who is watching this. Our audience is largely wannabe entrepreneurs in India. Okay. Really ambitious, really hungry, want to take the risk and build something. And I feel like all of us have so much to learn from you because you've done it so many times over in so many different domains. Yeah.
segments.textZh: 所以先让我说明一下，并交代一下观看者的背景。我们的观众主要是印度那些想成为创业者的人。好的。真的很有抱负，真的很渴望成功，想要承担风险并打造一些东西。而我觉得我们所有人都有太多东西可以向你学习，因为你已经在如此多不同领域里反复做成了这么多次。对。

segments.textEn: So, we will speak to them today, and I will try and centre all my questions in that direction so they can take advantage of this conversation and maybe start-- take a chance and build something. Okay, sure. Yeah, I guess the most important thing to do is just... make useful products and services. Yeah. Which one of all the products and services that you're building has got you most excited today?
segments.textZh: 所以，我们今天会对他们讲话，而我会尽量把所有问题都集中在那个方向上，这样他们就能从这次谈话中获益，也许会开始——冒一次险，打造一些东西。好的，当然。对，我想最重要的事情就是……创造有用的产品和服务。对。在你正在打造的所有产品和服务中，哪一个现在最让你兴奋？

segments.textEn: Well, I think that there's increasingly a convergence, actually, between SpaceX and Tesla and xAI. In that, if the future is solar-powered AI satellites, which it pretty much needs to be in order to... In order to harness a non-trivial amount of the energy of the sun, you have to move to solar-powered AI satellites in deep space... which, somewhat, is a confluence of Tesla expertise and SpaceX expertise. And xAI on the AI front, so...
segments.textZh: 嗯，我认为，SpaceX、Tesla 和 xAI 之间实际上正日益出现一种融合。也就是说，如果未来是太阳能驱动的 AI 卫星，而为了……为了利用数量不可忽视的太阳能量，基本上就必须如此，那么你就必须转向位于深空的太阳能驱动 AI 卫星……这在某种程度上是 Tesla 专长和 SpaceX 专长的汇合。再加上 xAI 在 AI 方面的能力，所以……

segments.textEn: it does feel like, over time, there's somewhat of a convergence there. But all the companies are doing great things. Very proud of the teams, they do great work. So, we're making great progress with Tesla on the autonomous driving. I don't know if you've tried the self-driving? -Mm-mm. -Have you tried it? I've tried it in the Waymo, not in the Tesla. Yeah, it's worth trying. We actually have it here in Austin. -So you can, like...
segments.textZh: 确实感觉随着时间推移，那里会出现某种融合。但所有公司都在做了不起的事情。我为这些团队感到非常自豪，他们的工作非常出色。所以，我们在 Tesla 的自动驾驶方面取得了很大进展。我不知道你有没有体验过自动驾驶？——没有。——你试过吗？我在 Waymo 里试过，在 Tesla 里没试过。对，值得一试。实际上，我们在奥斯汀这里就有。——所以你可以，比如……

segments.textEn: -Yeah, I'd love to try it. You can literally just download the Tesla app, and I think it's open to anyone. -Yeah. -Definitely try it out. You know how it goes. But we've made a lot of progress with electric vehicles, with battery packs and solar, and very much so with self-driving. So, basically, real-world AI. Tesla is the world leader in real-world AI, I would say.
segments.textZh: ——对，我很想试试。你真的只要下载 Tesla 应用程序就行，而且我想它对任何人都开放。——对。——一定要试试。看看效果怎么样。不过，我们在电动汽车、电池组和太阳能方面都取得了很大进展，自动驾驶方面尤其如此。所以，基本上就是真实世界 AI。我会说，Tesla 是真实世界 AI 的全球领导者。

segments.textEn: And then, we're gonna be making this robot, Optimus, which is starting production, hopefully, summer next year at scale. And I think that's gonna be pretty cool. That'll be like-- I think everyone's gonna want their own personal C-3PO, R2-D2, you know, a helper robot. Like, it would be pretty cool. And then, SpaceX is doing great work with the Starlink programme, providing low-cost, reliable Internet throughout the world. And hopefully, India.
segments.textZh: 然后，我们将制造这款机器人 Optimus，希望明年夏天开始规模化生产。而且我觉得那会非常酷。那会像是——我觉得每个人都会想拥有自己的私人 C-3PO、R2-D2，你知道，一个助手机器人。比如，那会非常酷。然后，SpaceX 的星链项目也做得非常出色，在全世界提供低成本、可靠的互联网。希望也能在印度提供。

segments.textEn: We'd love to be operating in India. That would be great. We're operating in 150 different countries, now, with Starlink. Can you give me a bit about Starlink and how the tech works? 'Cause somebody I was speaking to... I don't know if you know this company called Meter out of San Francisco. They're trying to replace network engineers. -But-- -Don't know it, no.
segments.textZh: 我们很希望能在印度开展业务。那会很棒。现在，星链已在 150 个不同国家开展业务。你能给我讲一点星链以及这项技术是如何运作的吗？因为我之前和一个人交谈……我不知道你是否知道一家来自旧金山、名叫 Meter 的公司。他们正试图取代网络工程师。——但是————不知道，没听过。

segments.textEn: So, he was telling me about how, in densely populated areas, Starlink works differently than it might be in a place with not as many people. Can you explain how it works? Yeah, so, Starlink... There's several thousand satellites in low-Earth orbit, and they're moving around 25 times the speed of sound in these... You know, they're zipping around the Earth, basically, and...
segments.textZh: 所以，他告诉我，在人口稠密地区，星链的运行方式与人口没那么多的地方可能不一样。你能解释一下它是如何运作的吗？可以，所以，星链……近地轨道上有数千颗卫星，它们正以约 25 倍音速在这些……你知道，它们基本上正飞速绕着地球运行，而且……

segments.textEn: they're at an altitude of about 550 kilometres, which is called, generally, low-Earth orbit. Because they're at low-Earth orbit there, the latency is low. Like, the distance, because the distance is not that far compared to a geostationary satellite at 36,000 kilometres. So, you've got thousands of satellites providing low latency, high-speed Internet throughout the world, and they are interconnected as well.
segments.textZh: 它们位于大约 550 公里的高度，这通常被称为近地轨道。因为它们在那里处于近地轨道，所以延迟很低。比如这个距离，因为与位于 36,000 公里高度的地球静止卫星相比，这个距离没有那么远。所以，你有数千颗卫星在全世界提供低延迟、高速互联网，而且它们彼此之间也相互连接。

segments.textEn: So, there are laser links between the satellites, so it forms, sort of, a laser mesh. So that the-- Let's say if cables are damaged or cut, like fibre cables, the satellites can communicate between each other and provide connectivity even if the cables are cut. So, for example, when the Red Sea cables were cut, I think, a few months ago, the Starlink satellite network continued to function without a hitch.
segments.textZh: 所以，卫星之间有激光链路，由此形成了某种激光网状网络。这样一来——假设电缆受损或被切断，比如光纤电缆，卫星可以彼此通信，即使电缆被切断也能提供连接。所以，举例来说，我想几个月前红海电缆被切断时，星链卫星网络仍然毫无障碍地继续运行。

segments.textEn: So, it's particularly helpful for disaster areas. So, if an area has been hit with some kind of natural disaster, floods or fires or earthquakes, that tends to damage the ground infrastructure. But the Starlink satellites still work, so... And generally, whenever there's of natural disaster somewhere, we always provide people with free Starlink Internet connectivity.
segments.textZh: 所以，它对灾区尤其有帮助。如果某个地区遭受了某种自然灾害、洪水、火灾或地震，那往往会破坏地面基础设施。但星链卫星仍然可以工作，所以……而且通常来说，只要某地发生自然灾害，我们总会为人们免费提供星链互联网连接。

segments.textEn: You know, we don't want to charge-- We don't want to take advantage of a tragic situation. So, it's always, you know, if there's natural disasters, we're like, "Okay, it's free during the natural disaster." You know, we don't want to, say, like, you know... put a paywall up while somebody's trying to get help. That would be wrong. So, it's a very robust system.
segments.textZh: 你知道，我们不想收费——我们不想利用悲剧性处境牟利。所以始终都是，你知道，如果发生自然灾害，我们就会说：“好的，自然灾害期间免费。”你知道，我们不想在某人正试图寻求帮助时，比如，你知道……设置一道付费墙。那样做是不对的。所以，这是一个非常稳健的系统。

segments.textEn: It's complimentary to ground systems because the satellite beams work best in sparsely populated areas. But because you've got a satellite beam, it's a pretty big beam, and you have a fixed number of users per beam, so... it tends to be very complimentary to the ground-based cellular systems, because those are very good in cities, because you've got these cell towers that are, you know, only a kilometre apart type of thing, but...
segments.textZh: 它与地面系统互为补充，因为卫星波束在人口稀少地区效果最好。但因为你使用的是卫星波束，它是一束相当大的波束，而每束波束能服务的用户数量是固定的，所以……它往往与地面蜂窝系统高度互补，因为地面蜂窝系统在城市里的表现非常好，因为那里有这些蜂窝基站，你知道，相互之间大概只隔 1 公里，但是……

segments.textEn: But cell towers tend to be inefficient in the countryside. So, in rural areas is where you tend to have the worst Internet because it's very expensive and difficult to lay... to do all the fibre-optic cables or to have high bandwidth cellular towers. So, Starlink is very complimentary to the existing telecom companies. It basically tends to serve the least served, which, I think, is good. -That's... -Will that change tomorrow?
segments.textZh: 但蜂窝基站在乡村地区往往效率不高。所以，农村地区往往是互联网最差的地方，因为铺设……铺设所有光纤电缆，或者建设高带宽蜂窝基站，都非常昂贵且困难。所以，星链与现有电信公司高度互补。它基本上倾向于服务那些最缺乏服务的人，我认为这很好。——那……——明天这会改变吗？

segments.textEn: Like, today, as you explained, the beam is quite broad, and it can't work in a densely populated area with high buildings, maybe. But can that change, and tomorrow, it becomes really efficient in a densely populated city where it is competitive with the local network providers? Unfortunately, the physics don't allow for that. So, we're too far away. So, at 550 kilometres, even if we try to reduce it, which...
segments.textZh: 比如，今天，正如你所解释的，波束相当宽，而且它可能无法在人口稠密、高楼林立的地区运行。但这能改变吗？到了明天，它在一个人口稠密的城市里变得非常高效，足以与当地网络提供商竞争？遗憾的是，物理规律不允许这样。所以，我们离得太远了。所以，在 550 公里的高度，即使我们试图降低这个高度，而这……

segments.textEn: About as low as we can go is about 350 kilometres, still very far away. You've just... You can think of, like, a flashlight, which is, you know, this flashlight's got a cone and that cone is coming at, you know... today, it's 550 kilometres. In the future, we're trying to get down to 350 kilometres, but we can't beat something that's one kilometre away, which is the cell tower. Physics is not on our side here.
segments.textZh: 我们最低大约能降到 350 公里，仍然非常遥远。你刚刚……你可以想象一下，比如一支手电筒，也就是，你知道，这支手电筒有一个锥形光束，而那个锥形光束正朝着……你知道……如今是 550 公里。未来，我们正努力降到 350 公里，但我们无法击败距离只有 1 公里的东西，也就是通信基站。物理规律在这件事上对我们不利。

segments.textEn: So, it's not physically possible for Starlink to serve densely populated cities. Like, you can serve a little bit, maybe 1% of the population. And, sometimes, people get-- Even in crowded cities, there might be, you know, no fibre link up their road. Like, sometimes, there's somebody on a cul-de-sac or something or in a place... In cities, there's sometimes underserved areas for random reasons.
segments.textZh: 所以，从物理上说，星链不可能为人口稠密的城市提供服务。比如，你可以服务一小部分，也许是人口的 1%。而且，有时人们会——即使在拥挤的城市里，他们所在的道路可能也没有光纤连接。比如，有时有人住在死胡同之类的地方，或者住在某个地方……在城市里，有时会因为各种偶然原因而存在服务不足的地区。

segments.textEn: And so, Starlink can serve, like I said, maybe 1% or 2% of a densely populated city. But it can be much more effective in, like I said, in rural areas where the Internet connection is much worse. And often, people either have, sometimes, no access to Internet or it's extremely expensive or the quality is not very good.
segments.textZh: 所以，星链可以像我说的那样，为人口稠密城市中也许 1% 或 2% 的人提供服务。但它在农村地区可能有效得多，就像我说的，那里的互联网连接要差得多。而且人们往往要么有时根本无法接入互联网，要么费用极其昂贵，要么质量不太好。

segments.textEn: If I were to ask you to wager a guess, Elon, do you think India will go down the path of urbanisation like China did, with more people moving in from rural economies to urban centres? Or do you think we'll beat the trend? Well, I suppose some amount of that has happened, right? I mean, I'm curious to, sort of, ask you some questions as well. 'Cause, of course, isn't that the trend, or is it not the trend in India? It is the trend, largely.
segments.textZh: 如果让我请你大胆猜测一下，埃隆，你认为印度会像中国那样走上城市化道路，让更多人从农村经济地区迁往城市中心吗？还是你认为我们会打破这种趋势？嗯，我想其中一部分已经发生了，对吧？我的意思是，我也很好奇，想问你一些问题。因为，当然，这不是趋势吗，还是说这在印度并不是趋势？总体而言，这是趋势。

segments.textEn: I think a little bit changed during COVID when a lot of urbanisation slowed down and that was not organic. It was very artificially manifested. Right. But one does question that with AI, if productivity were to go up... And I heard you speak about UHI instead of UBI. Yeah. I think it will be Universal High Income.
segments.textZh: 我认为新冠疫情期间情况略有变化，当时很多城市化进程放缓了，而那并不是自然发生的。那是非常人为地造成的。对。但随着 AI 的发展，如果生产率提高，人们确实会思考这个问题……而且我听到你谈过用 UHI 取代 UBI。是的。我认为会是全民高收入。

segments.textEn: In a world like that, I wonder if more people want to live in cities which are always going to be more polluted and not offer the quality of lifestyle that a rural environment might. Well, I guess it's up to... Some people want to be around a lot of people and some people don't. It's gonna be, maybe, a matter of personal choice. But I think in the future, it won't be... I think it won't be the case that you have to be in a city for a job. -Right.
segments.textZh: 在那样的世界里，我想知道是否会有更多人想住在城市里，而城市总会污染更严重，也无法提供农村环境或许能够提供的生活品质。嗯，我想这取决于……有些人想待在很多人身边，有些人则不想。这也许会是个人选择的问题。但我认为未来不会……我认为不会再出现为了工作而必须待在城市里的情况。——对。

segments.textEn: -'Cause I think... My prediction is, in the future, working will be optional. Right. We seem to be moving from-- Not in India, but in some parts of the West, from six days to five days to four days to three. Not me. [laughter] I think, the Europeans. Yeah, yeah. Yeah, yeah, 'cause...
segments.textZh: ——因为我认为……我的预测是，未来工作将是可选的。对。我们似乎正在从——不是在印度，而是在西方的一些地区，从每周工作 6 天变成 5 天，再变成 4 天、3 天。我不是。[笑声]我觉得是欧洲人。是的，是的。是的，是的，因为……

segments.textEn: I mean, I think if you're trying to make a startup succeed or you're trying to make a company do very difficult things, then you definitely need to put in serious hours. -I think that's how it goes. -Right. And if we were to move from five to four to three days, how do you think society changes? When people have to work half the week, what do they do with the other half? Well, I think it'll actually be that people don't have to work at all.
segments.textZh: 我的意思是，我认为如果你试图让一家初创企业取得成功，或者试图让一家公司去做非常困难的事情，那么你肯定需要投入大量时间。——我觉得事情就是这样。——对。如果我们从每周 5 天变成 4 天，再变成 3 天，你认为社会会发生怎样的变化？当人们只需工作半周时，另外半周会做什么？嗯，我认为实际上会变成人们根本不必工作。

segments.textEn: What did DOGE teach you, if you learnt one thing? Well, it was like a very interesting side quest, you know, 'cause I just got to see like a lot of inner workings of the government. And, you know, there's been quite a few efficiencies.

Then on the right, you've got, you know, at least a perception that somehow their jobs are being taken by talented people from other countries. I don't know how real that is. My direct observation is that there's always a scarcity of talented people.
segments.textZh: 你知道，某个人——他们是什么情况并不重要，他们可能是罪犯，也无所谓。然后在右翼这边，你会看到，至少有一种看法认为，他们的工作不知怎么正被来自其他国家的人才抢走。我不知道这在多大程度上是真的。我的直接观察是，人才始终是稀缺的。

segments.textEn: So, from my standpoint, I'm like, "We have a lot of difficulty finding enough talented people to get these difficult tasks done. And so more talented people would be good." But I guess, some companies out there, it's sort of, they're making it more of a cost thing, where it's like, okay, if they can employ someone for a fraction of the cost of an American citizen, then, I guess, these other companies would hire people just to save costs.
segments.textZh: 所以，从我的角度来看，我会说：“我们很难找到足够多的人才来完成这些困难的任务。因此，有更多人才会是好事。”但我猜，外面有些公司更把这当成成本问题，类似于，好吧，如果他们能以美国公民用工成本的一小部分雇用某个人，那么我猜，这些其他公司会仅仅为了节省成本而雇人。

segments.textEn: But, at my companies, the issue is we just are trying to get the most talented people in the world. And we pay way above average. So I can't say-- So, that's not my experience. But that's what a lot of people do complain about. And I think there's been some misuse of the H-1B Program. It would be accurate to say that there's, like, some of the outsourcing companies have kind of gamed the system on the H-1B front.
segments.textZh: 但在我的公司里，问题是我们只是在努力招揽全世界最有才华的人。而且我们支付的薪酬远高于平均水平。所以我不能说——所以，那不是我的经历。但这确实是很多人抱怨的事情。我认为H-1B项目存在一些滥用。可以准确地说，有些外包公司在H-1B方面钻了制度的空子。

segments.textEn: And we need to stop the gaming of the system, you know? But I'm certainly not in the school of thought that we should shut down the H-1B Program. That's-- Which some on the right are. I think they don't realise that that would actually be very bad. If you could speak to the people of my country, India, the young entrepreneurs who want to build... -Right. -... and say a message to them, what would you say?
segments.textZh: 而且我们需要制止对这个制度的钻营，你知道吗？但我当然不属于那种认为我们应该终止 H-1B 项目的人。那是——右翼中的一些人持有的观点。我认为他们没有意识到，那实际上会非常糟糕。如果你可以对我的国家印度的人民说话，对那些想要打造……的年轻创业者们——对。——……并向他们传达一条信息，你会说什么？

segments.textEn: I'm a big fan of anyone who wants to build. So I think anyone who wants to... you know, make more than they take, has my respect. So that's the main thing you should aim for, aim to make more than you take. Be a, you know, a net contributor to society. And it's kind of like the pursuit of happiness. You know, if you want to create something valuable financially, you don't pursue that.
segments.textZh: 我非常欣赏任何想要打造东西的人。所以我认为，任何想要……你知道，创造多于索取的人，都值得我的尊重。所以这是你应该追求的主要目标，要以创造多于索取为目标。成为一个，你知道，对社会有净贡献的人。这有点像对幸福的追求。你知道，如果你想创造某种在经济上有价值的东西，你不能去追求那个。

segments.textEn: It's best to actually pursue providing useful products and services. If you do that, then money will come as a natural consequence of that, as opposed to pursuing money directly. Just like you can't, sort of, pursue happiness directly, you pursue things that lead to happiness. But there's not like direct happiness pursuit. You do things like... I guess, fulfilling work, or study, or friends, loved ones, that, as a result, make you happy.
segments.textZh: 最好是真正去追求提供有用的产品和服务。如果你这样做，那么金钱就会随之自然到来，而不是直接追逐金钱。就像你无法算是直接追求幸福一样，你要追求那些会带来幸福的事物。但并不存在类似直接追求幸福这种事。你会做一些事情，比如……我想，有成就感的工作、学习、朋友、挚爱之人，这些事情最终会让你幸福。

segments.textEn: So, it sounds very obvious... but, generally, if somebody's trying to make a company work, they should expect to grind super hard, accept that there's, like, some meaningful chance of failure, but just be focused on having the output be worth more than the input. That are you a value creator? That's what really matters. Making more than you take. I think that's a good way to end this. -Lauren is asking us to wrap up. -All right.
segments.textZh: 所以，这听起来非常显而易见……但是，一般来说，如果有人正努力让一家公司运转起来，他们应该预期要极其努力地苦干，接受存在着某种不容忽视的失败可能性，但只专注于让产出比投入更有价值。也就是你是不是一个价值创造者？那才是真正重要的。创造多于索取。我觉得这样结束很好。——Lauren 在让我们收尾。——好的。

segments.textEn: I also like to take the opportunity to thank my friend, Manoj, in IGF. He does a great job of connecting, I think, Indians, like the group here, with people like you, in order to... of many things, I think, get to know each other and become friends, because once we are friends, maybe we can start working together. So, thank you, Manoj, for putting this whole thing together, and thank you, IGF.
segments.textZh: 我也想借此机会感谢我在 IGF 的朋友 Manoj。我认为，他很好地把像这里这个群体一样的印度人和像你这样的人联系起来，以便……在许多事情当中，我想，让彼此相互了解并成为朋友，因为一旦我们成为朋友，也许就能开始一起合作。所以，感谢 Manoj 促成这一切，也感谢 IGF。

segments.textEn: [audience applauding] And, thank you so much, Elon, for taking the time. You're welcome. -Did you have fun? Was it boring? -Yeah, it was an interesting conversation. Sometimes, they take these answers out of context. But... I think it was a good conversation.
segments.textZh: [观众鼓掌] 还有，非常感谢你抽出时间，埃隆。不客气。-你聊得开心吗？无聊吗？-是的，这是一次有意思的对话。有时，他们会断章取义地截取这些回答。但是……我认为这是一次很好的对话。
